captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 7. In this lesson: Stronger than a thousand storms.
Identify hyperbole and other figurative language.
Here are some new words. Hyperbole. Extreme exaggeration for effect. Figurative.
Not meaning exactly what the words say. Literal. Meaning exactly what the words say.
And some more words. Effect. The feeling or idea a writer creates in a reader. Exaggerate.
Make something seem bigger or worse than it is. Vivid. Creating clear, strong pictures in the mind.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: extreme exaggeration for effect?
Now some grammar: Literal or figurative? Literal language means exactly what it says.
Figurative language (metaphor, simile, personification, hyperbole) creates a picture or feeling.
For example: Literal: I am very hungry. For example: Figurative (hyperbole): I could eat a horse!
Now listen, and read along. My little brother. My little brother is a hurricane,
He spins through every room; He's louder than a thousand drums, A one-boy sonic boom.
He eats enough for twenty men, His laughter shakes the floor, He's slower than a snail asleep When Mum says,
‘Shut the door!’ But when the night is dark and long And thunder starts to fall,
He creeps into my bed and says, ‘You're not afraid at all.’
Another question. The video will stop. What is the little brother compared to in line 1?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like hyperbole, figurative, literal.
You practised literal or figurative language. And you read My little brother. Now try the practice questions.
See you next time!

q.prompt: What is the rhyme scheme of the first four lines?

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 7. In this lesson: Rhythm and rhyme.
Recognise rhyme schemes and how rhythm affects a poem.
Here are some new words. Rhythm. A regular pattern of strong and weak beats. Rhyme scheme.
The pattern of rhymes at the ends of lines, for example A, B, A, B. Stanza.
A group of lines in a poem; a verse.
And some more words. Repetition. Using the same word or phrase again. Mood. The feeling a poem creates.
Couplet. Two lines that rhyme together.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: a regular pattern of strong and weak beats?
Now some grammar: Rhyme scheme. Use letters to show which line endings rhyme.
Lines that rhyme get the same letter. For example: cat, A. Dog, B. Hat, A. Log, B.
So the pattern is A, B, A, B.
Now listen, and read along. The market drum.
Beat the drum and sound the call, Bring the baskets, one and all!
Mangoes, melons, rice and beans, Silver fish and juicy greens. Beat the drum and clap your hands,
Here come traders from far lands, Selling silk and copper bowls, Spices, songs and honey rolls.
Beat the drum – the sun is low, Pack the baskets, time to go.
Another question. The video will stop. What is the rhyme scheme of the first four lines?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like rhythm, rhyme scheme, stanza. You practised rhyme scheme.
And you read The market drum. Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
